title: CELPIP Speaking: The Eight Tasks
summary: CELPIP's eight recorded speaking tasks — from giving advice to describing a scene — and the prep-then-speak routine that keeps you fluent.

nodes.label: Advice & experience
nodes.note: Give advice; describe a personal experience

nodes.label: Opinions & unusual
nodes.note: Express opinions; describe an unusual scene

nodes.label: Prep then speak
nodes.note: Short prep, then record your answer

chunks.heading: Eight recorded tasks, prep then speak
chunks.body: Speaking has **eight tasks**, each with a **short preparation time and then a recording time** — you speak into the microphone, there's no examiner. The tasks include **Giving Advice, Talking about a Personal Experience, Describing a Scene, Making Predictions, Comparing and Persuading, Dealing with a Difficult Situation, Expressing Opinions, and Describing an Unusual Situation**.
chunks.realExample: You get a few seconds to plan, then a fixed window to talk — so a quick mental outline (point, reasons, close) matters more than a perfect script you can't finish.
chunks.memoryHook: 8 tasks, each: short prep → record. Plan fast, then keep talking to the buzzer.

chunks.heading: Describe a Scene & Describe an Unusual Situation
chunks.body: For the picture tasks, **describe what you see systematically** — location, people, actions, details — filling the whole time. In 'unusual situation', you also **explain what's odd or what might be happening**. Keep a steady flow; naming details fluently is what scores.
chunks.realExample: Describe a park scene left-to-right or foreground-to-background so you never run dry: 'In the foreground… behind them… in the distance…' — a spatial order fills the time naturally.
chunks.memoryHook: Describe in a spatial order (front → back). Detail by detail fills the whole window.

chunks.heading: The opinion & persuasion tasks
chunks.body: For **Giving Advice, Comparing and Persuading, Expressing Opinions**, use a clear mini-structure: **state your position, give reasons with examples, and address the other side**. Sound natural and confident — the goal is real communication, not memorised phrases.
chunks.realExample: Comparing two options? 'I'd choose X because… and although Y has an advantage, X wins overall because…' — a structure that persuades in 60 seconds.
chunks.memoryHook: Position → reasons + example → address the other side. Persuade, don't recite.

chunks.heading: Fluency and clarity beat a perfect accent
chunks.body: Human raters reward **clear, natural, fluent speech that fully addresses the task** — not a particular accent or big vocabulary. **Don't go silent**: if you lose your thread, rephrase and continue. Use the full recording time.
chunks.realExample: Blanking mid-answer? Say 'Another point is…' and pivot to a fresh reason rather than trailing off — recovering smoothly protects your fluency score.
chunks.memoryHook: Clear, natural, complete — and never silent. Fill the whole recording window.

recall.q: How many speaking tasks does CELPIP have, and is there an examiner?
recall.a: Eight tasks, each with short prep then recording — you speak into a microphone with no examiner.

recall.q: Name several of the CELPIP speaking task types.
recall.a: Giving Advice, Talking about a Personal Experience, Describing a Scene, Making Predictions, Comparing and Persuading, Dealing with a Difficult Situation, Expressing Opinions, and Describing an Unusual Situation.

recall.q: How should you approach the 'Describe a Scene' task?
recall.a: Describe systematically in a spatial order (e.g. foreground to background), naming details fluently to fill the whole time.

recall.q: What structure works for the opinion/persuasion tasks?
recall.a: State your position, give reasons with examples, and address the other side.

recall.q: What do CELPIP speaking raters reward most?
recall.a: Clear, natural, fluent speech that fully addresses the task — not a particular accent or advanced vocabulary.
